subject: Retrospective billing adjustment: withholding tax applied to US invoices / ledger request
messages:
From: Aisha Kapoor <accounts@novaplay.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Discrepancy on Nov invoices — withholding tax applied

Hi Vivek,

We've been reconciling our November statements and noticed Redwood applied a 10% withholding tax to a set of US invoices (Invoice #1142, #1143). That withholding reduced the net payment reported on our end and the amounts don't match our remittance file. Can you confirm why withholding tax was applied to these invoices?

We need:
- A short ledger/line-item export for the three invoices showing gross, tax, net, and any applied withholding.
- Confirmation if Redwood can issue a credit (or refund) for the withheld portion if it was applied in error.

This is urgent for our year-end audit — appreciate a quick turnaround. I'm copying Legal for visibility.

Thanks,
Aisha Kapoor
Finance Lead
NovaPlay Inc.

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 10:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Nov invoices — withholding tax applied

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the patience — we completed the ledger review. Please see the attached CSV snapshot that maps our invoice lines to accounting entries. Summary:

- Invoice 1142 (dated 2026-11-01): Gross $123,456.70 — a 10% withholding (labeled WH Tax) of $12,345.67 was applied at billing time.
- Invoice 1143 (2026-11-15): Gross $45,000.00 — no withholding applied.

Root cause: During a migration from an older reseller configuration, a legacy tax rule mistakenly flagged NovaPlay's account for withholding on certain invoice templates. That rule should not have applied to US corporate customers with tax residence on file.

Remediation proposed:
1) Issue a credit memo for $12,345.67 against Invoice 1142 (credit memo attached as PDF).
2) Offer to apply the credit to your next invoice (Jan 2027) or process a refund to the bank account listed on your remittance advice. Please indicate preference.
3) To avoid recurrence, please provide a completed tax residency declaration (we've attached instructions). Once we receive the signed form we'll mark your account so withholding is not applied going forward.

Attachments included: credit_memo_1142.pdf, tax_residency_form_instructions.pdf, invoice_1142-ledger-snapshot.csv

If you'd prefer a direct wire for the credit, we'll need the beneficiary details (account name, routing/IBAN, SWIFT). Alternatively we can offset the Jan invoice immediately.

Apologies for the inconvenience — happy to expedite once we get your preferred path.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Kapoor <accounts@novaplay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Nov invoices — withholding tax applied

Hi Marissa / Vivek — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear explanation.

We accept the credit memo for $12,345.67 and would prefer Redwood apply the credit to our January 2027 invoice rather than process a refund. That will simplify our cashflow.

Attached is the remittance stub with the bank reference (novaplay_remittance_dec20.pdf). We'll have Legal sign the tax residency declaration and return it by Jan 5. Please confirm the credit is applied to the Jan invoice and let me know the invoice number that will be reduced so our AP team can match.

Appreciate you resolving this ahead of year-end.

Best,
Aisha Kapoor
Finance Lead
NovaPlay Inc.
